title: With BHAC15 contraction radii, the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio explains the age decline of the CPV rate in 763 TESS M-dwarf rapid rotators, and no extra age term is necessary
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period, probably from material near the corotation radius R_cor. An earlier result found that, at a fixed period P, the CPV rate falls from 16% at 15-24 Myr to 2% at 89-200 Myr (e-folding time 44 Myr). We tested whether stellar contraction causes this decline: at a fixed P, a smaller star has a larger x = R_cor/R*. We used the same 763 BANYAN Sigma members (75 CPVs; TESS sectors 56-107, P = 0.15-1 d, BP-RP = 2.4-3.8) and the same efficiency correction. R* is the BHAC15 radius at the group age (R_iso) or the Stefan-Boltzmann radius from Gaia photometry (R_sb). At a fixed x, the age classes have the same rate, and the rate falls as x^(-6.5 +/- 1.4) above x = 2. With R_iso, a model with no age parameter fits as well as the free 44-Myr model; an extra age term has p = 0.76 and tau > 75 Myr. A model fitted to 1-24 Myr stars predicts 14.2 (10.4-18.8) CPVs in older classes with x, and 54.6 with P; we observe 17. With a free intercept per class, CPV periods become shorter with age (median 0.53, 0.45, 0.32, 0.28 d) as contraction predicts (radius exponent 1.08, 0.75-1.48; no shift rejected, p = 5e-4). With R_sb the residual age term is weak (p = 0.053), and a height-based test without kinematic ages agrees. Thus contraction is sufficient to explain the decline, and the 44-Myr scale need not be a material lifetime. Limitations: one automated vetter made the labels; only 17 CPVs are older than 35 Myr; the radius scale depends on models; with P = 1-2 d stars or R_sb in a narrow window the shift test or the age term changes; a smaller residual age effect is not excluded.

display.caption: Efficiency-corrected CPV rate per rapid rotator in three BANYAN age classes (763 members, 75 CPVs). (a) At a fixed rotation period the rate falls with age. (b) At a fixed x = R_cor/R* with the BHAC15 radius at the group age, the classes agree. (c) The same with the photometric Stefan-Boltzmann radius. Bins with fewer than 8 stars are not shown; bars are 95% Poisson intervals.

(a) Profile of an extra exponential age term: with period as the rotation variable the best e-folding time is 44 Myr; with x the age term is not needed (dotted lines: no age term). (b) Period-shift test with a free intercept per age class (spline shape): gamma = 1 is pure x control, gamma = 0 means the same CPV periods at all ages. (c) Median period of the CPVs in each class, observed and expected under x control and under a fixed-period shape (quadratic shape); numbers give CPVs/window rapid rotators.

Rotation period and stellar radius of the window rapid rotators (small dots) and CPVs (large symbols) by age class, with lines of constant x = R_cor/R* for 0.17 solar masses. Left: BHAC15 radius at the group age (small random offsets for display). Right: photometric radius.

citations.reason: Reuses its BANYAN age classes and injection efficiencies. Its 44-Myr decline at fixed period is reproduced, but we show that stellar contraction (x = R_cor/R*) is sufficient to explain it, so the time scale need not be a material lifetime.

Uses its CPV labels, periods and Gaia photometry. Our result gives a physical reason for its height trend: stars high above the main sequence are large, so their corotation radius is close to the star.
The height association at fixed period follows from the radius dependence of x.
Fixed-density transit geometry; we let the stellar radius change and find a much steeper x dependence than a transit chance.
